items.title: Positive Breakout: These 7 stocks cross above their 200 DMAs
items.description: In the Nifty 500 pack, seven stocks gained over 1% and their closing prices crossed above their respective 200-day moving averages (DMA) on November 20, 2026, according to StockEdge's technical scan data. The 200-day moving average (DMA) is used by traders as a key indicator for determining the overall trend of a stock. As long as a stock's price remains above its 200-day moving average on the daily timeframe, it is generally interpreted as being in an overall uptrend.

items.title: Page Industries nears 52-week low as weak sales growth spooks investors
items.description: Page Industries has witnessed a sharp decline in its share prices, approaching a 52-week low, driven by disappointing sales volume growth. Analysts are growing wary about the company's prospects for achieving double-digit volume increases for FY27, especially with current trends. The operating margin has slipped to 20.8% due to rising input costs.

items.title: Select HFCs offer rate cuts, top-ups to retain borrowers
items.description: As competition among lenders intensifies, housing finance firms are deploying a range of tactics to secure their customer base. These include attractive interest rate discounts and personalized offers designed to minimize mortgage transfers. Home First Finance is witnessing a drop in balance-transfer outflows as a result of these strategic actions. However, despite improved retention through analytics-driven methods, the industry faces ongoing significant net balance-transfer outflows each month.

items.title: Sensex surges 20% in dollar terms as foreign money chases India
items.description: The Sensex has increased by 20% in dollar terms this quarter, marking a potential bull market. Foreign fund flows have contributed significantly to this surge, driven by global investors seeking diversification. The rupee's appreciation has also enhanced returns for foreign investors holding Indian assets. Despite recent gains, many investors remain cautious and have yet to fully engage in the Indian market.

items.title: D-Street poised for a gap-up start as GIFT Nifty trades firmly higher
items.description: Indian stock markets experienced a robust upswing on Friday, driven by a surge in domestic purchases against a backdrop of weaker global trends. The banking sector emerged as a key player, pushing weekly gains to 5.9%. Market experts foresee the Nifty index climbing towards record highs, likely crossing the 25500 mark, with this level serving as a potential support point.

items.title: Stocks in news: Adani Energy, Maruti Suzuki, RailTel, Waaree Energies and Indian Bank
items.description: Indian equity benchmarks ended higher on Friday, driven by a rally in private banking stocks. The Nifty 50 index rose by 286 points, approaching a critical technical resistance level. Adani Energy Solutions, Maruti Suzuki India, and several other companies are expected to be in focus on Monday. Key developments include share acquisitions, price increases, and capital-raising plans from various firms.

items.title: Nifty eyes 26,300 as analysts favour banking, auto and realty stocks
items.description: Analysts anticipate a continued upward trend for the Nifty index, targeting levels around 26,000 to 26,300. Recommended strategies include buying on dips while being cautious due to overbought indicators. Key stocks include Federal Bank, Apollo Hospitals, and HDFC Life, among others. The Bank Nifty remains a favored investment due to its relative strength and momentum. Investors are advised to favor large-cap stocks amidst selective participation in the market.

items.title: FPIs turn aggressive buyers, invest Rs 1.18 lakh crore into Indian equities in November
items.description: Foreign portfolio investors have become net buyers of Indian equities, making substantial investments in November. They have invested over ₹1.18 lakh crore so far, indicating a strong market reversal. Previously, FPIs were net sellers, offloading equities worth around ₹5.51 lakh crore from October 2024 to mid-October 2026. The recent buying trend has occurred over 13 consecutive trading sessions, averaging around ₹1,450 crore per hour.

items.title: Chandrasekaran to push Tata Sons IPO plan at board meet, company valued at up to Rs 18 lakh crore
items.description: Tata Sons is working on a public listing plan that may value the holding company at ₹18 lakh crore. Chairman N Chandrasekaran will present the IPO proposal at the upcoming board meeting. This move follows the Reserve Bank of India's directive for a listing without delay due to existing regulatory requirements. Investment banks, including Bank of America, are involved in the IPO process preparations.

items.title: Mahindra Finance scouts gold loan firms for acquisition, evaluates four potential targets
items.description: Mahindra & Mahindra Financial Services is exploring acquisitions of gold finance companies to diversify its revenue streams. Among the targets are Indel Money, Kosamattam Finance, ICL Fincorp, and Supra Pacific Financial Services. Discussions have begun, but no formal offers have been made at this stage. The company aims to increase its presence in the growing gold loan market while maintaining its vehicle financing operations.

items.title: Stock Radar: Bharti Airtel rallies 14% in a month; multi-month triangle breakout signals further upside
items.description: Bharti Airtel has broken out of a multi-month triangle pattern on the weekly charts, signalling further upside potential. The stock has rebounded sharply after finding support above Rs 1,700 in September and is nearing fresh record highs. Experts recommend medium-term buying, with a target of Rs 2,400 over the next 3-4 months.

items.title: Banks warn higher costs could hit demand as RBI weighs further repo hike
items.description: Bank executives held consultations with Reserve Bank of India officials regarding inflation risks and capital formation challenges. They expressed concern that higher interest rates may affect consumption demand due to rising costs. Particular attention was given to stress in sectors such as agriculture and gold loans. India's gold loan market saw non-performing assets rise significantly in recent months.

items.title: Tata Steel clears sale of two units to APL Apollo
items.description: Tata Steel has decided to sell its tubes business and Tata Steel Colours in two transactions valued at ₹28,000 crore. APL Apollo Tubes will acquire the tubes unit and Tata Steel Colours, with completion expected by March 31, 2028. The tubes unit generated a turnover of approximately ₹11,375 crore while Tata Steel Colours reported around ₹4,680 crore in revenue.

items.title: Tech Mahindra announces record date for 1:1 bonus issue. Check details
items.description: Tech Mahindra has fixed November 30 as the record date for its 1:1 bonus share issue, with the new shares set to be available for trading from December 2. Eligible shareholders will receive one additional share for every share held. The announcement follows shareholder approval and strong September-quarter earnings.

items.title: India Inc Q2 earnings hit 12-quarter high: Will it fuel the next bull run on D-Street?
items.description: Indian companies recorded their strongest earnings growth in 12 quarters in Q2FY27, with Nifty-500 sales, EBITDA and PAT rising 25%, 24% and 32%, respectively. Metals, oil and gas and financials led the recovery, while smallcaps outperformed. Motilal Oswal remains constructive on equities amid improving earnings momentum.

items.title: Robert Kiyosaki loads up on gold, silver, Bitcoin amid crash fears. Here’s why
items.description: Robert Kiyosaki is buying physical gold, silver, Bitcoin, Ethereum, real estate and oil, citing concerns over the Federal Reserve, US debt and the global financial system. The Rich Dad Poor Dad author has warned that an impending crash could be worse than 2008, while advising investors to wait for Bitcoin to bottom.

items.title: Bloodbath in APL Apollo shares: How much worse can the fall be and what should investors do?
items.description: APL Apollo Tubes plunged after Tata Steel announced plans to acquire a controlling stake, with investors concerned about the Rs 28,000-crore acquisition burden, promoter exit and valuation of the combined business. Tata Steel shares also fell over 9% as investors assessed the financial implications, despite the strategic rationale of combining the two companies' steel tubes and downstream businesses.

items.title: Stock Market Holiday: Are BSE, NSE closed on November 24 for Guru Nanak Jayanti?
items.description: The BSE and NSE will remain closed on November 24 for Guru Nanak Jayanti, while MCX trading will be suspended during the morning session and resume in the evening. This will be the second-last stock market holiday of 2026, with the next closure scheduled for Christmas on December 25. Indian equities are meanwhile nearing record highs amid strong FII buying.

items.title: 5 stocks with consistent score improvement and upside potential of up to 27% in 1 year, according to analysts
items.description: Forget what the indices are doing. At this point of time, focus on risk management; and also ensure that, when you put money in the market, the company you are targeting has sound fundamentals. And at the sector level, check whether there is any structural change.

items.title: Premier Explosives rallies 11% on Rs 311 crore international order for manufacture and supply of defence explosives
items.description: Premier Explosives shares rallied on Monday after the defence manufacturer secured a Rs 311 crore export order for the manufacture and supply of defence explosives. The 12-month contract comes amid strong quarterly revenue growth, a sharp rise in EBITDA and an order book of Rs 1,642 crore.

items.title: APL Apollo Tubes effect: Multibagger SG Mart shares soar 14% on fundraising plans. What’s the link?
items.description: SG Mart shares rallied after the company scheduled a board meeting to consider fundraising plans. The development comes amid Tata Steel's proposed acquisition of a controlling stake in APL Apollo Tubes, whose promoter group is led by the Sanjay Gupta family.

items.title: The great Indian stock market comeback. Can the rally sustain and what should investors do?
items.description: Indian equities staged a sharp 9.7% rally in eight sessions through November 12, reversing months of underperformance. A sell-off in US AI stocks, triggered by Republican losses in the midterm elections and fears of tighter AI regulation, spilled across global technology markets. Earlier, foreign investor outflows, elevated crude prices and rupee weakness had weighed heavily on Dalal Street sentiment.

items.title: Nifty Bank drops over 2% after scaling lifetime high; Union Bank and PNB among top losers
items.description: Bank Nifty fell 2% after its recent record-high rally, with Union Bank, Bank of Baroda and Canara Bank leading losses. Profit booking across banking stocks dragged the index lower, while analysts expect near-term weakness without fresh triggers.

items.title: The great rotation begins! India’s MSCI EM weight jumps to 14.7% after two years of heavy FII selling
items.description: India’s weight in the MSCI Emerging Markets index has climbed to 14.7%, gaining four percentage points since October 1, as global investors rotate away from crowded AI trades. Nearly $16 billion in foreign equity inflows since October 16 has fuelled the reversal after two years of heavy FII selling.

items.title: Why did market fall today? Sensex crashes 1,484 pts, Nifty ends below 25,350. Key factors behind Rs 5 lakh crore selloff
items.description: The stock markets faced a significant blow on Monday as Nifty and Sensex plummeted, reflecting intense selling pressure in multiple sectors. Investors suffered a colossal loss of Rs 5.24 lakh crore in wealth, driven by declines in heavyweight stocks like HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank. Coupled with worries about rising interest rates from the US Fed and a weakening rupee, this situation has led to a cautious atmosphere among investors.

items.title: TCS, Infosys, Wipro, other IT stocks rise up to 3% as AI bloodbath continues; Nasdaq logs worst week since 2020
items.description: Indian IT stocks bucked the global tech selloff, with the Nifty IT index rising over 700 points. TCS, Wipro, Infosys, HCL Tech and Tech Mahindra gained, while Coforge and Persistent Systems also advanced. The gains came even as AI-linked concerns triggered sharp losses in US tech stocks.

items.title: Ashoka Buildcon shares jump 7% after securing projects worth over Rs 4,200 crore from NHAI and Rajasthan Metro
items.description: Ashoka Buildcon shares rose after the company secured projects worth over Rs 4,200 crore, including an NHAI expressway contract and two Jaipur Metro projects for which it emerged as the lowest bidder in a joint venture with SAM India.

items.title: Tata Steel shares fall 9% as investors assess the impact of APL Apollo buyout
items.description: Tata Steel shares fell sharply as investors assessed its Rs 15,510.6 crore deal to acquire a 26.38% stake in APL Apollo Tubes and launch an open offer. The proposed transaction will combine downstream businesses to create a 7.5 million tonne steel tubes and colour-coated products platform.

items.title: Nifty, Sensex within striking distance of record highs. Will FIIs keep buying after ₹1.3 lakh crore inflows?
items.description: The Nifty and Sensex indices are nearing their historic peaks, buoyed by a remarkable streak of 15 consecutive days of purchasing by foreign institutional investors, amassing over ₹1.3 lakh crore in Indian stocks this month. While this surge is encouraging, inflation still looms large, with the Retail Price Index on the rise.
